assessment.name: Involved-360
assessment.description: A competency based 360-evaluation that provides an analytically robust picture of strengths and improvement opportunities.
assessment.instructions:
INSTRUCTIONS - PLEASE READ CAREFULLY

​The dimensions below are designed to provide developmental feedback to strengthen leadership.  Please use the scales below to indicate your ratings for [name] on the following performance dimensions.  

First read the dimension and then review all of the descriptors for a given dimension. These are example descriptions to help you better understand dimension levels. 

Each dimension ranges from ‘below expectations’ to ‘exceeds expectations'. You will notice that under ‘below expectations’, ‘meets expectations’, and ‘exceeds expectations’ there are several statements that define performance at these respective levels. The ratings for ‘slightly below expectations’ and ‘slightly exceeds expectations’ do not have descriptions but would be a mix of the descriptions immediately to the left and right. Please select the rating that is most accurate for [name] based upon your experience with [name]. 

Third, you are highly encouraged to include examples of observed or documented behaviors to aid in the developmental feedback process. Please provide additional detail to help [name] develop as a leader. Only provide information that you have observed - do not report stories or interpretations or things that might be considered 'gossip'.

questions.content:
Creative Problem Solving

Definition: Creative Problem Solving is defined as proactive problem-solving focusing on the successful implementation of novel and creative solutions to known or anticipated problems, being mindful of and efficient in using resources (i.e., resourcefulness), and utilizing a visionary mindset.

Please select your rating for [name] for this dimension.
Your rating for Creative Problem Solving:

Lacks creativity when trying to solve existing problems


Sometimes develops creative solutions to navigate problems


Always seeks innovative solutions to problems

Consistently fails to utilize talent to improve processes, advance procedures, or execute tasks


Implements novel solutions to existing problems with some success


Consistently implements creative solutions to existing challenges with high success

Fails to follow through with executing new ideas/initiatives  as promised


Notices when change is necessary


Implements new/improved processes or procedures to navigate obstacles

Typically satisfied with following the same routines/processes over extended periods of time




Consistently educates self in areas of expertise and seeks out new knowledge in unfamiliar areas

Highly resistant to change




Takes positive action, even in the face of unforeseen obstacles, and works to overcome traditional boundaries to move ahead in day-to-day activities as well as long-term activities.
Developmental Comments for Creative Problem Solving:

Leadership Adaptability

Definition: Leadership Adaptability is having the ability to see the need for change early on. Having the willingness to smoothly and comfortably adjust his/her work style to the change as well as assist his/her team in positively adapting to the change. This competency also captures one's psychological ownership over the change.

Please select your rating for [name] for this dimension.
Your rating for Leadership Adaptability:

Fails to make changes happen even after being asked to do so by trusted advisors or superiors


Makes changes happen without significant negative impact when asked to do so 


Takes ownership of changes and creates a positive change atmosphere

Does not react well to changing environments and fails to maneuver him/herself in a manner that generates productive outcomes


Reacts well to changing environments and minimizes stress on others


Has the ability to see change coming and actively maneuvers him/herself to create a positive outcome

Handles change poorly, creating a negative environment for others


Generally supports change


Acts as an advocate for change to others facing difficult circumstances



Handles change well without creating a negative environment for others


Volunteers to be an active participant in groups or tasks where change is expected
Developmental Comments for Leadership Adaptability:

Collaboration

Definition: Collaboration is being able to effectively work with internal stakeholders/employees up and down the chain of organizational hierarchy (vertical) and horizontally with peers as well as external individuals/organizations/partners (e.g., vendor, community leaders) all the while knowing and showing ones authentic self to others at work while simultaneously knowing how one is portrayed across all work settings. 

Please select your rating for [name] for this dimension.
Your rating for Collaboration:

Focus is solely on his/her own work and/or function


Interfaces on occasion with peers and utilizes information learned to improve


Interfaces purposely with peers and utilizes information learned to improve

Does not seek to develop relationships with others


Develops relationships with a few others (peers/colleagues) and occasionally assists others



Develops strong relationships with others (peers/colleagues) and assists others in understanding objectives and achieving results

No focus on community partnerships. Views partners as resources that are disposable


Maintains solid, respected relationships



Interfaces with community members by volunteering to cultivate valuable relationships

Eschews relationships to serve own interests, “goes it alone”, lacks interest in others opinions and expertise


Interfaces with community members to create valuable relationships


Builds networks with key leaders, peers, and/or colleagues who can provide expertise and serve as trusted “go-to’s”

Disruptive to relationships


Has solid relationships with peers, colleagues, and superiors (e.g., teachers).


Utilizes relationships to move forward significant tasks and projects and create successful outcomes
Developmental Comments for Collaboration:

Self-Development

Definition: Self-Development encompasses identification of weaknesses and positive action to overcome identified weaknesses, continuing to build one's strengths, being self-aware of actions and how they impact others, transferring formal and informal training/development back to one's daily job, and mastering all aspects of management, not just functional expertise.

Please select your rating for [name] for this dimension.
Your rating for Self-Development:

Comfortable in their own skin, overly satisfied with current state


Attends training as required for new activities related to their area in the organization and demonstrates applied learning


Actively evaluates their current skill set and identifies weaknesses/creates improvement plans to then correct and strengthen those areas without negative impact to strengths

Defiant when faced with feedback. Provides counter reasoning rather than accepting coaching


Works with their supervisor to improve on areas that they are weak to be more successful in their current role


Seeks feedback on regular basis pertaining to soft skills. Actively works to develop new approaches and communication styles

Unwilling to learn new skills or avoids learning opportunities which are challenging or uncomfortable


Is able to introduce some of the new skills into daily work routine


Seeks out challenging learning opportunities (webinars, conferences, higher ed) to develop new technical skills, specifically in areas of weakness and abilities to grow in the areas required for their next career step

Mandatory training is rarely completed on time for self and supervised staff


Ensures any mandatory training is completed timely for self and staff


Works with supervisor to create development plans in order to advance their job knowledge/skill set





Implements new acquired knowledge into new skills and applies them directly to their job
Developmental Comments for Self-Development:

Performance Management

Definition: Performance Management is defined as the ability to consistently lead and develop individuals and teams, set goals, create and implement a valued rewards structure, consistently hold individuals and teams accountable in an effective and positive manner, and provide the necessary information in a clear and actionable manner.

Please select your rating for [name] for this dimension.
Your rating for Performance Management:

Weak team building skills. Not skilled at holding underperforming members accountable. Plays favorites


Builds a good team and holds most others accountable for their performance


Develops a strong team by identifying the best people for the task/job and assertively holds underperforming members accountable

Goal development is not tied to or considerate of team members’ objectives


Ability to structure goals that are considerate of others’ objectives


Ability to structure robust goals that align with others’ objectives and ensures goals properly support broader objectives 

Takes little effort to connect team goals with individual team members’ interests or skills


Utilizes team members’ talents to advance performance


Properly identifies others who have the ability to develop into more impactful contributors and assists in their development
Developmental Comments for Performance Management:

Business Mindset

Definition: Business Mindset encompasses having a clear and complete focus on the organization as a sustainable/growing business, seeing and implementing the entire vision of the organization, inclusive of internal and external stakeholders, and linking departmental/unit operations to all business indicators (i.e., labor costs, customer satisfaction, quality), and how departmental/unit metrics truly impact the entire business.

Please select your rating for [name] for this dimension.
Your rating for Business Mindset:

Does not fully understand how he/she can impact personal and career outcomes by implementing change


Has a general understanding of how he/she can impact personal and career outcomes by implementing change


Has a strong command of cause-effect relationships that impact personal and career outcomes by implementing change

Comfortable with the status quo


Able to adjust some to support overarching personal and professional objectives for individual, unit, and organizational success


Embraces challenges requiring adjustment to accomplish overarching personal and professional objectives for individual, unit, and organizational success

Only concerned about his/her immediate surroundings and generally only thinks about near-term (rather than long-term) consequences of actions


Concerned about how immediate actions impact others and thinks about intermediate consequences of actions for him/herself, unit, and the entire business


Incorporates the consequences of his/her actions on others into his/her decision making and focuses on the long-term consequences of action for him/herself, unit, and the entire business
Developmental Comments for Business Mindset:

Customer Focus

Definition: Customer Focus encompasses anticipating, communicating, and addressing current & emerging customer needs; actively listening to customers’ needs, goals, and expectations; developing, reinforcing and strengthening customer service culture; adjusting priorities to meet multiple and often competing customers’ demands, seeks and incorporates feedback from customers to improve performance, and follows up with customers to insure needs have been met satisfactory. This competency applies to both internal and external customers.​

Please select your rating for [name] for this dimension.
Your rating for Customer Focus:

Consistently fails to provide assistance and information to others or begrudgingly provides minimal service; fails to identify or solve service issues; does not learn from past mistakes


Willingly provides assistance and useful information to meet needs; assumes ownership of issues and takes appropriate steps to correct problems


Anticipates needs and goes beyond normal duty to provide service; takes ownership of issues; actively seeks ways to improve service; makes useful improvement suggestions to the appropriate stakeholder

Consistently fails to greet others promptly and be polite in interactions


Greets others promptly and respectfully in person and by phone; listens attentively to verify needs


Provides necessary information that a person needs even if the person does not know exactly what to ask for; anticipates needs and resolves issues before situations require action

Is not attentive or considerate of other’s needs


Quickly establishes and maintains positive relationships


Maintains a professional demeanor at all times when serving others

Fails to leave a positive impression with customers; inappropriately reacts to situations; consistently damages customer relationships


U​sually takes an interest and understands customer needs; shows respect by remaining patient, calm and polite


Highly attentive to needs, even during busy periods, of all customers, internal and external

Does not answer questions in an understandable way; has difficulty identifying resources that could enhance customers' experiences or needs


Meets needs by acting professionally and applying a good working knowledge of available services and information to all customers


Consistently behaves in a respectful and diplomatic fashion to diffuse difficult situations with all customers
Developmental Comments for Customer Focus:

Communication

Definition: Communication is defined as clearly, concisely, and accurately conveying necessary information when it is needed while avoiding sharing unfounded information/rumors. Communication also encompasses providing rationale behind messages/decisions; seeking to understand others views and priorities, adjusting communication styles to audience, and encouraging open and candid dialogue from others.​

Please select your rating for [name] for this dimension.
Your rating for Communication:

Ineffectively expresses thoughts, whether orally or in writing


Expresses thoughts clearly, both orally and in writing


Communication is of the highest caliber; clear, persuasive, accurate, and focused on the needs of specific individuals and groups

Fails to demonstrate effective listening skills via distraction, disinterest, over reactive response, interruption and/ or somewhat inaccurate restatement of others’ view


Demonstrates effective listening skills by being attentive and focused


Consistently demonstrates highly effective and tailored writing and speaking styles to convey messages and ideas to varied audiences to build understanding, commitment and organizational effectiveness

Does not ask questions or share knowledge and information to help others clearly understand processes and desired results


Asks questions and shares knowledge and information to help others clearly understand processes and desired results


Consistently exhibits earnest listening and consideration to build trust and confidence while carrying input forward to appropriate parties

Fails to give and receive helpful and timely feedback


Gives, receives and acts upon helpful and timely feedback


Consistently models highly effective behaviors in sharing knowledge and information that propels and teaches others to perform in like manner

Often appears distracted or disinterested; frequently interrupts others; contributions are often unclear or inaccurate


Effective communicator; knowledgeable and concise; actively listens to and synthesizes perspectives of others


Highly proficient communicator; listens to and synthesizes others’ ideas; explains even complex issues clearly and succinctly
Developmental Comments for Communication:

Ethics & Integrity

Definition: Ethics & Integrity competency is defined as instilling mutual trust & confidence, building and reinforcing inclusivity for all, accepting/owning responsibility for mistakes and successes, creating a culture that fosters high standards of integrity & ethics, behaves in a fair, just, and ethical manner to all stakeholders, shows consistency in principles, values, and behaviors, and demonstrates a sense of responsibility and commitment to the organization, colleagues, and all customers.​

Please select your rating for [name] for this dimension.
Your rating for Ethics & Integrity:

Lacks transparency in communications and in actions; shows little to no regard nor respect for others 


Demonstrates transparency in communications and in actions; shows regard and respect for others most of the time


Demonstrates transparency in communications and in actions; shows high regard and respect for others

Fails to follow guiding ethical principles of the organization; behaves in selfish manner


Consistently follows guiding ethical principles of the organization


Consistently and without exception, follows guiding ethical principles of the organization and integrates with personal principles

Does not understand nor follow organizational policies and practices with integrity; fails to demonstrate concern for ethical behavior; and is an example of poor ethical behavior


Understands and follows policies and practices with integrity; usually demonstrates a genuine concern for ethical behavior; and is occasionally a role model for others


Clearly understands and follows policies and practices with integrity, without exception; is highly principled demonstrating a concern for ethical behavior; is a role model for other team members

Fails to help others understand, appreciate, and follow guiding ethical principles with unwavering integrity


Occasionally helps others understand, appreciate, and follow guiding ethical principles with unwavering integrity


Often, and almost without exception, helps others understand, appreciate, and follow guiding ethical principles with unwavering integrity

Encourages others to turn a ‘blind eye’ to organizational policy and ethical guidelines
Developmental Comments for Ethics & Integrity:
